name: xcode
description: Work with Xcode projects from Kimi Code: build, run, and test schemes, render SwiftUI previews, drive simulators and devices, read build logs and diagnostics, manage project files, and search Apple developer documentation — via Xcode's built-in MCP server (xcrun mcpbridge), the same integration Apple ships for Claude Code.
author: kimi-xcode-plugin (MCP server and skills by Apple, exported from Xcode)

interface.shortDescription: Build, test, and run Xcode schemes; SwiftUI previews; simulators; build logs; Apple docs
interface.longDescription:
Gives Kimi Code direct access to Xcode through the MCP server built into Xcode itself (xcrun mcpbridge) — the same machinery behind Apple's official Claude Code plugin (xcode@claude-plugins-official).

Capabilities:
- Build, run, and test schemes (BuildProject, RunProject, RunAllTests, RunSomeTests)
- Render SwiftUI previews (RenderPreview)
- Drive simulators and devices: boot, install, launch, synthesize input (DeviceInteraction*)
- Read build logs, console output, crash and diagnostics logs (GetBuildLog, GetConsoleOutput, Get*IssueLogs)
- Browse and edit the project: list schemes/targets/workspaces, read/write files inside the project, glob/grep/ls/mv/rm (Xcode*)
- Manage build settings, entitlements, Info.plist, compiler flags
- Work with String Catalogs (localization)
- Search Apple developer documentation (DocumentationSearch)

Prerequisites: macOS with Xcode installed; open the project/workspace in Xcode before asking the agent to work with it; allow external agents in Xcode Settings → Intelligence (Xcode shows an alert when an agent connects). After updating Xcode, re-run scripts/export-from-xcode.sh and reinstall the plugin to refresh the bundled skills.
